meta.title: David's 3-week meal plan
notes: Plan weeks run Friday to Thursday: David shops first thing on Friday and the week starts when he gets home.
No microwave and no toaster. Rice pouches are used cold, straight from the pouch. Toast bread in a dry frying pan.
Macros are approximate, from typical UK per-100g values.
Saturday lunch and dinner are free meals; aim to include some protein.
rules: Avoid energy drinks, sugar spikes and skipped meals
Excluded: whey, prawns, lamb, tinned salmon. Tinned tuna max 1 tin a week
Opened rice pouch halves: fridge, eat within 48 hours
Always check the actual use-by date in store
Nothing needs defrosting: frozen fish is cooked from frozen and frozen bread is toasted from frozen

ingredients.note: Staple: enter how many you have before shopping

ingredients.note: Opened half: fridge, eat within 48 hours

ingredients.name: Sourdough, San Francisco loaf
ingredients.note: Slice it when you get home: keep half out, freeze half for Week 3. Toast from frozen.

ingredients.name: Baby / new potatoes
ingredients.note: Keeps 2 weeks somewhere cool and dark; can carry over

ingredients.name: Bananas

ingredients.note: 400g jar; an opened jar lasts more than a week

ingredients.name: Mixed nuts, unsalted
ingredients.note: Max 2 to 3 Brazil nuts a day

recipes.name: Skyr bowl

ingredients.note: steel-cut, soaked overnight in a splash of water

method: The night before: soak 40g oats in a splash of water in the fridge.
In the morning, spoon 300g skyr into a bowl.
Top with the soaked oats, 100g frozen berries straight from the freezer and 20g pumpkin seeds.

recipes.name: Overnight oats with banana
method: The night before: mix 60g steel-cut oats with 284ml milk (half a pint) in a jar and refrigerate.
In the morning, stir, top with sliced banana, 150g skyr and 15g pumpkin seeds.
Boil 1 egg for 9 minutes (or use one boiled the night before) and eat on the side.
recipes.prepAhead: Soak oats in milk the night before

recipes.name: Scrambled eggs, smoked salmon & sauerkraut
method: Toast 1 slice of sourdough in a dry frying pan, about 3 minutes each side (from frozen is fine).
Scramble 3 eggs gently in 5ml olive oil over a low heat.
Serve the eggs on the toast with 100g smoked salmon and 50g sauerkraut on the side. Glass of kefir (250ml) on the side.

recipes.name: Post-parkrun eggs & smoked salmon
method: Toast 2 slices of sourdough in a dry frying pan, about 3 minutes each side (from frozen is fine).
Wilt 80g spinach in a pan with 5ml olive oil, then scramble 3 eggs.
Serve with 100g smoked salmon and an orange.

recipes.name: Banana + coffee (pre-parkrun)
method: Eat a banana with your usual small coffee about 90 minutes before parkrun.

recipes.name: Banana (pre-badminton)
method: Eat a banana around 4:30pm to fuel badminton.

recipes.name: Tuna & butter bean salad
method: Boil 2 eggs for 9 minutes, cool and halve.
Drain and rinse 1 tin butter beans; drain 1 tin tuna.
Chop a little red onion and add 50g mixed leaves.
Toss everything with 10ml olive oil, the juice of half a lemon, salt and pepper.

recipes.name: Chicken, white rice & kimchi bowl
method: Uses chicken steamed on Monday evening.
Warm the chicken in a pan until piping hot, or eat it cold.
Tip 1 white basmati pouch into a bowl, cold, straight from the pouch. Add the chicken and top with 80g kimchi.

recipes.name: Chicken, brown rice & kimchi bowl
method: Uses chicken steamed on Monday evening.
Warm the chicken in a pan until piping hot, or eat it cold.
Tip half a brown basmati pouch into a bowl (the other half is for tonight's dinner), cold, straight from the pouch. Add the chicken and top with 80g kimchi.

recipes.name: Turkey chilli with white rice
method: Uses the second chilli portion, batch-cooked on Wednesday evening.
Reheat one portion in a pan until piping hot.
Serve over 1 white basmati pouch, cold, straight from the pouch.

recipes.name: Turkey chilli with brown rice
method: Batch-cook the chilli this evening: brown 500g turkey mince, add 1 chopped onion, ¾ pepper, 2 garlic cloves, cumin, paprika, chilli, 1 tin kidney beans and 1 tin tomatoes; simmer 25 minutes. Makes 2 portions.
Eat one portion now with the other half of the brown basmati pouch, cold, straight from the pouch.
Cool the second portion quickly and fridge it for Thursday lunch.

recipes.name: Chicken & butter bean salad
method: Steam 200g chicken breast for 20–25 minutes until cooked through; slice.
Boil 1 egg for 9 minutes. Drain and rinse 1 tin butter beans.
Toss with 50g mixed leaves, a little chopped red onion, 10ml olive oil and lemon juice.

recipes.name: Salmon traybake
method: Steam 200g baby potatoes and 2 frozen salmon fillets (200g), straight from frozen, for 15 to 18 minutes.
Add 150g tenderstem broccoli for the last 6 to 7 minutes.
Season and finish with lemon juice.

recipes.name: Thai-style steamed beef & green beans
method: Mix 250g beef mince with 2 crushed garlic cloves, the grated ginger and the chilli flakes; spread it in a shallow heatproof dish and steam for 15 to 20 minutes, until no pink remains.
Add the sliced onion, pepper and 100g green beans to the steamer for the last 6 to 7 minutes.
Break it up with a fork and pour off any fat. Toss everything with 15ml soy sauce and the lime juice.
Serve over 1 white basmati pouch, cold, straight from the pouch.

recipes.name: Chicken traybake with sweet potato
method: Heat oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Cut 250g sweet potato into chunks; toss with 1 sliced pepper, red onion, 10ml oil and paprika. Roast 15 minutes.
Add 250g chicken breast, cut into chunks, and roast a further 20 minutes until cooked through.

recipes.name: Steamed cod & potatoes
method: Steam 250g baby potatoes and 2 frozen cod fillets (200g), straight from frozen, for 12 to 15 minutes.
Add 150g tenderstem broccoli and 80g frozen peas for the last 6 to 7 minutes.
Drizzle 5ml olive oil and lemon juice over the potatoes; season.

recipes.name: Beef bolognese
method: Put 250g beef mince in a shallow heatproof dish and steam for 15 to 20 minutes, until no pink remains. Break it up with a fork and pour off any fat.
Meanwhile, cook the chopped onion, grated carrot and 2 garlic cloves gently in a splash of water for 5 minutes.
Add 1 tin chopped tomatoes, the herbs and the steamed mince; simmer for 15 minutes.
Cook 100g wholewheat spaghetti and serve with the sauce.

recipes.name: Roast chicken dinner
method: Heat oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Halve 250g baby potatoes, toss in 10ml oil, roast 35 minutes.
Roast 250g chicken breast for the last 20–25 minutes.
Steam 100g tenderstem broccoli and 100g green beans.

recipes.name: Cottage cheese on rye
method: Toast 2 slices of rye bread in a dry frying pan, about 3 minutes each side (from frozen is fine).
Top with 300g cottage cheese and a sliced tomato; season with black pepper.
2 boiled eggs on the side (boil the night before to save time).

recipes.name: Apple & cinnamon overnight oats
method: The night before: mix 60g steel-cut oats, 250ml kefir, a splash of water, 1 grated apple and cinnamon. Refrigerate.
In the morning, top with 150g skyr and 15g walnuts.
1 boiled egg on the side.

recipes.name: Feta omelette
method: Fry 80g sliced mushrooms in 5ml oil for 3 minutes; add 80g spinach and let it wilt.
Whisk 3 eggs with 165g egg whites; pour over the veg and cook on medium-low.
Crumble 40g feta over, fold, and serve with 1 slice of rye. Glass of kefir (250ml) on the side.

recipes.name: Post-parkrun feta omelette
method: Same as the feta omelette, with 2 slices of rye and an orange instead of kefir.

recipes.name: Egg & lentil salad
method: Boil 3 eggs for 9 minutes; cool and quarter.
Tip 1 lentil pouch into a bowl (cold is fine).
Add 50g mixed leaves and a chopped tomato, and crumble over 40g feta.
Dress with 5ml olive oil and lemon juice.

recipes.name: Lemon-oregano chicken, white rice & sauerkraut
method: Uses chicken steamed on Monday evening with lemon, oregano and garlic.
Tip 1 white basmati pouch into a bowl, cold, straight from the pouch.
Add the chicken, 80g sauerkraut and a dollop of skyr (75g).

recipes.name: Lemon-oregano chicken, brown rice & sauerkraut
method: Uses chicken steamed on Monday evening with lemon, oregano and garlic.
Tip half a brown basmati pouch into a bowl (the other half is for tonight's dinner), cold, straight from the pouch.
Add the chicken, 80g sauerkraut and a dollop of skyr (75g).

recipes.name: Beef & black bean bowl with white rice & kimchi
method: Uses the second portion, batch-cooked on Wednesday evening.
Reheat the beef in a pan until piping hot.
Serve over 1 white basmati pouch (cold, straight from the pouch) with 80g kimchi on top.

recipes.name: Beef & black bean bowl with brown rice & kimchi
method: Batch-cook the beef this evening: mix 300g beef mince with cumin and paprika and steam it in a shallow dish for 15 to 20 minutes; break it up, pour off any fat and stir in 1 tin black beans. Makes 2 portions.
Eat one portion now with the other half of the brown basmati pouch, cold, straight from the pouch, and 80g kimchi on top.
Cool the second portion quickly and fridge it for Thursday lunch.

recipes.name: Lemon trout with crushed potatoes
method: Steam 200g baby potatoes for 15 minutes.
Add 2 trout fillets and 200g green beans for the last 8–10 minutes.
Lightly crush the potatoes with 5ml olive oil, lemon juice and salt.

recipes.name: Chicken thigh curry
method: Trim 300g chicken thighs and cut into chunks.
Brown the chicken in a dry non-stick pan (thighs release their own fat); remove.
Soften chopped onion in the same pan; add garlic, ginger and 2 tsp curry powder for 1 minute.
Return the chicken with sliced pepper; add 1 tin tomatoes; simmer 20 minutes.
Stir in 240g spinach until wilted. Serve with 1 white basmati pouch, cold, cold, straight from the pouch.

recipes.name: Pork loin with sweet potato & sauerkraut
method: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Roast 200g sweet potato chunks with 5ml oil for 30 minutes.
Season the pork loin steaks with paprika and pan-fry for 4 to 5 minutes each side, until cooked through.
Serve with 80g sauerkraut.

recipes.name: Beef meatballs with spaghetti
method: Mix 200g beef mince with finely grated onion, 1 garlic clove and herbs; roll into 8 balls.
Steam the meatballs for 12 to 15 minutes, until cooked through.
Meanwhile, simmer 1 tin tomatoes with the other garlic clove for 10 minutes. Add the meatballs and simmer for 5 minutes more.
Cook 80g wholewheat spaghetti and serve.

recipes.name: Chicken & chickpea tagine
method: Trim 300g chicken thighs and cut into chunks.
Brown the chicken in a dry non-stick pan; add chopped onion, garlic and 2 tsp ras el hanout.
Add 1 tin chickpeas and 1 tin tomatoes; simmer 25 minutes.
Pour boiling water over 60g couscous, cover 5 minutes, fluff and serve.

recipes.name: Steamed sirloin steak with roasted veg
method: Halve 200g baby potatoes; roast with pepper and courgette in 5ml oil at 200°C for 30 minutes.
For the last 10 minutes, steam the sirloin: 8 to 10 minutes for medium (a little less for pink, a little more for well done).
Rest the steak for 5 minutes before slicing.

recipes.name: Quark bowl
method: The night before: soak 30g oats in a splash of water.
Spoon 300g quark into a bowl; top with the oats, 100g frozen raspberries straight from the freezer and 20g almonds.

recipes.name: Banana oat pancakes
method: Blitz 60g steel-cut oats to a flour.
Blend with 2 eggs, 200g quark, 1 banana and cinnamon.
Cook small pancakes in a non-stick pan with a little oil, 2 minutes each side.
Top with 125g quark. On Tuesday cook both days' batches and fridge Thursday's.

recipes.name: Shakshuka
method: Uses the shakshuka sauce batch (2 tins tomatoes, 2 peppers, 1 onion, garlic, cumin, paprika, 15ml oil, simmered 20 minutes; makes 3 portions).
Heat one portion in a small pan. Stir in 165g egg whites, then make 4 wells and crack in 4 eggs.
Cover and cook on low for 6–8 minutes until set.
Toast 1 slice of sourdough in a dry frying pan, about 3 minutes each side (from frozen is fine). Serve with a glass of kefir (165ml).

recipes.name: Post-parkrun shakshuka
method: As shakshuka, with 2 slices of sourdough and an orange.

recipes.name: Cottage cheese & quinoa protein bowl
method: Steam 80g frozen edamame for 3–4 minutes.
Tip 1 quinoa pouch into a bowl; add 300g cottage cheese, sliced cucumber and the edamame.
Squeeze over lemon; season.

recipes.name: Lemon-herb chicken, bulgur & sauerkraut
method: Uses chicken and bulgur cooked on Monday evening.
Warm in a pan until piping hot, or eat it cold as a salad.
Drizzle with 10ml olive oil and serve with 80g sauerkraut.

recipes.name: Lemon-herb chicken, bulgur & sauerkraut
method: Uses chicken and bulgur cooked on Monday evening.
Warm in a pan until piping hot, or eat it cold as a salad.
Drizzle with 10ml olive oil and serve with 80g sauerkraut.

recipes.name: Beef larb with white rice
method: Uses the second larb portion, batch-cooked on Wednesday evening.
Reheat in a pan until piping hot; stir through fresh mint, coriander and spring onion.
Serve in little gem leaves with 1 white basmati pouch, cold, straight from the pouch.

recipes.name: Beef larb with brown rice
method: Batch-cook the larb this evening: steam 500g beef mince with garlic and chilli in a shallow dish for 15 to 20 minutes; break it up, pour off any fat, and finish with fish sauce and lime. Makes 2 portions.
Eat one portion now with fresh mint, coriander and spring onion, in little gem leaves, with 1 brown basmati pouch, cold, straight from the pouch.
Cool the second portion quickly and fridge it for Thursday lunch.

recipes.name: Steamed sea bass with ginger
method: Steam 200g baby potatoes for 10 minutes.
Lay 2 sea bass fillets on top with shredded ginger and spring onion; add 80g edamame. Steam 8–10 minutes.
Drizzle with 10ml soy sauce and 5ml oil.

recipes.name: Honey-garlic chicken
method: Cut 200g chicken breast into chunks; fry in 5ml oil for 8 minutes.
Add 2 crushed garlic cloves, 15g honey and 15ml soy; bubble 2 minutes until sticky.
Steam 200g tenderstem broccoli. Serve with 1 white basmati pouch, cold, cold, straight from the pouch.

recipes.name: Turkey steaks with sweet potato
method: Steam 250g sweet potato chunks for 15 minutes; add 250g shredded greens for the last 5.
Season the turkey steaks with paprika; pan-fry in 5ml oil 4–5 minutes each side until cooked through.

recipes.name: Salmon & kimchi noodles
method: Steam 2 frozen salmon fillets (200g), straight from frozen, for 15 to 18 minutes, then flake.
Cook 60g wholewheat noodles and drain.
Toss the noodles with 80g kimchi, 15ml soy sauce, the salmon and sliced spring onion.

recipes.name: Chicken arrabbiata
method: Fry 150g chicken chunks in 5ml oil for 6 minutes; remove.
Soften onion and garlic; add chilli flakes and 1 tin tomatoes; simmer 15 minutes.
Return the chicken; cook 5 minutes. Toss with 100g cooked wholewheat penne.

recipes.name: Steamed rump steak with chimichurri
method: Steam 200g baby potatoes for 15 minutes. Lay the rump steak on top for the last 8 to 10 minutes (medium), and add 200g green beans for the last 6.
Chimichurri: finely chop 15g parsley and 1 garlic clove; mix with 10ml olive oil, 10ml vinegar and chilli.
Rest the steak for 5 minutes, slice it and spoon over the chimichurri.

recipes.name: Steamed chicken (Tue/Wed lunches)
method: Steam the chicken breasts for 20 to 25 minutes, until there's no pink in the middle. If your steamer has room, put it in with tonight's dinner.
Let it cool, slice it, split it into 2 tubs (150g each) and fridge them for Tuesday and Wednesday lunch.

recipes.name: Turkey chilli (2 portions)
method: Heat the oil in a large pan and brown the turkey mince, breaking it up.
Add the chopped onion, pepper and crushed garlic and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the cumin, paprika and chilli flakes, then the kidney beans and tomatoes.
Simmer for 25 minutes, stirring now and then.
Eat one portion tonight. Cool the other quickly and fridge it for Thursday lunch.

recipes.name: Lemon-oregano chicken (Tue/Wed lunches)
method: Toss the chicken with the lemon juice, oregano, garlic and a pinch of salt.
Steam for 20 to 25 minutes, until there's no pink in the middle. If your steamer has room, put it in with tonight's dinner.
Let it cool, slice it, split it into 2 tubs and fridge them for Tuesday and Wednesday lunch.

recipes.name: Burrito beef (2 portions)
method: Mix the beef mince with the cumin and paprika, then spread it in a shallow heatproof dish and steam for 15 to 20 minutes, until no pink remains.
Break it up with a fork and pour off any fat.
Stir in the drained black beans; put the dish back in the steamer for 3 minutes to warm them through.
Eat one portion tonight. Cool the other quickly and fridge it for Thursday lunch.

recipes.name: Shakshuka sauce (3 portions)
method: Heat the oil in a pan. Slice the onion and peppers and cook gently for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the crushed garlic, cumin and paprika and cook for 1 minute.
Add both tins of tomatoes and simmer for 20 minutes.
Let it cool, split it into 3 tubs and fridge them. Each tub is one shakshuka breakfast.

recipes.name: Lemon-herb chicken and bulgur (Tue/Wed lunches)
method: Toss the chicken with the lemon juice, oregano and a pinch of salt.
Steam for 20 to 25 minutes, until there's no pink in the middle. If your steamer has room, put it in with tonight's dinner.
Meanwhile put the bulgur in a pan with 300ml boiling water, cover and simmer gently for 10 minutes, then leave it covered off the heat for 5 minutes.
Let it cool and split it into 2 tubs: half the chicken in each, with a slightly bigger share of bulgur in Tuesday's. Fridge them.

recipes.name: Banana oat pancakes (double batch)
method: Blitz the oats to a flour.
Blend with the eggs, quark, bananas and cinnamon.
Cook small pancakes in a non-stick pan with a little oil, 2 minutes each side.
Eat half now, topped with 125g quark. Cool the rest and fridge it for Thursday.

recipes.name: Beef larb (2 portions)
method: Mix the beef mince with the garlic and chilli flakes, then spread it in a shallow heatproof dish and steam for 15 to 20 minutes, until no pink remains.
Break it up with a fork and pour off any fat.
Stir in the fish sauce and lime juice.
Eat one portion tonight. Cool the other quickly and fridge it for Thursday lunch.

recipes.name: Handful of mixed nuts
method: Eat a handful (30g) with lunch. No more than 2 to 3 Brazil nuts a day.
